Summary calibration:

  • A and B: closed questions in practice; confidence effectively 1 for any decision that matters.
  • C: settled at the level of "the extraordinary claim has not met its burden of proof, and a mundane explanation has"; not settled at the level of "we have positively excluded the exotic." Turn-4 quantification: the surviving record is worth 2.4:1 to 222:1 against the exotic claim, i.e. 71–99.5 % mundane (§5.5). Anyone holding below ~70 % must be treating the Mogul track reconstruction, the material match, and the 1997 test-dummy attribution as carrying essentially zero weight.
  • D: settled at the level of "no extraterrestrial cause has been demonstrated and natural mechanisms suffice"; the residual doubt about a non-terrestrial actor is not resolvable by evidence that currently exists, and I regard the claim as unfalsifiable in its current form — which is itself a mark against it, not a mark in its favour. Turn-4 quantification: even a composite LR of $10^{-2}$ (ten orders of magnitude more charitable than my assignment) with a $10^{-3}$ prior leaves $10^{-5}$; reaching a coin flip requires prior odds of $10^{12}\!:\!1$.

7. What remains unknown for each claim

  • A. Nothing material. The residual unknowns are only pedagogical: which stadion Eratosthenes used (157.5 vs 184.98 m), which is a units ambiguity, not a geometry one. Turn 7: every [CALC] number in §1 is now machine-verified; the only defect found (E-1, a 5×-under-stated local-flatness figure) is corrected, and the claim now carries eleven independent tests, the newest being implied ground speeds (A-8b).
  • B. Nothing material. After the turn-3 verification pass the residual unverified items were narrow — per-mission skin dosimetry, exact heat-flow site values, per-mission sample masses to ±0.05 kg, Bochum/Jodrell reception specifics — none load-bearing (see §9 and Appendix B). Turn 5 closed the heat-flow site values (A15 ≈ 21, A17 ≈ 16 mW/m²) and the Van-Allen transit time (§9c), and turn 6 closed the per-mission dosimetry completely from the open primary record (§2.5, §9d), leaving only the ≤2.6 % Apollo 12/14 sample-mass convention conflicts and the Bochum-amateur reception details — all [LIT], none load-bearing. **As of turn 6, claim (b) has zero [LIT-verify] numbers left: every quantity in §2 is either [GT], [CALC], or confirmed against an open source. Turn 7 re-verified all of them numerically and found two of my own defects (E-2/E-3, the star-exposure cross-check; E-5, the conflict label), both now fixed. Turn 8 closed the last open item in the claim: the Bochum reception is no longer a bare [LIT-verify] assertion but a sourced, instrument-specific record (20 m dish, Apollo 11 + Apollo 16, videotape still in storage, primary citation Kaminski, Neues von Rohde & Schwarz 57:24–27, 1972), and the third-party tracking paragraph has been replaced by a 13-nation table (§2.3 B-4). The single genuinely open item is the cause** of the 0.85–1.15 kg gap between the sum of the six per-mission masses and the primary-confirmed 382 kg total — that needs the JSC curator's per-mission table (or Papike, Ryder & Shearer, Rev. Mineral. Geochem. 36, ch. 5, 1998, which the open third-party survey cites as its source for the total), and it cannot move the total.
  • C. One genuine unknown (narrowed in turn 9 from two). (1) Whether a complete set of 1947-era classified records exists anywhere unsearched. The GAO/Congressional investigations of the 1990s found no documentary evidence of a crash-recovery programme, and the 1994 report checked the AFHRA / AFSA / NARA holdings and the USAF crash database for the 24 June – 28 July 1947 window (five crashes: A-26C, P-51N, C-82A, P-80A, PQ-14B — none on the date or in the area), but that is a search, not an audit. **Turn 9 note: this unknown is now worth less than turn 4 assumed, because the 1994 report's own finding that no air-safety records exist for weather-balloon crashes at all means the null result is the benign model's prediction — the "no records" branch no longer discriminates between hypotheses.** (2) The actual composition of the 1947 debris is no longer an unknown in the operative sense: the 9 July 1947 inventory is good enough to identify it quantitatively (2.27 kg of rubber, paper, tape and sticks over 182.88 m), which is why the debris sub-claim moved from "absence" to "corroborated mundane" in turn 9. (Turn 4: the assigned-LR decomposition in §5.5 shows the second unknown was worth less than a factor of ~2.4 to the final answer, whereas my item-level judgement implied ~222 — so the "no records exist" branch is not where the disagreement lives.)
  • D. The mechanism for the individual case (which specific sleep-state disturbance, which specific source-monitoring failure) is unresolved case-by-case. That is not a worry about the class conclusion: the population-level naturalistic explanation is established, and the extraterrestrial one is not. Turn 8 adds one specific open sub-item: the 2021 lucid-dream emulation study is cited at second hand (the journal site is behind an anti-bot challenge and ResearchGate refused the request), so its exact N, recruitment method and scoring rubric are unread here; the direction of its result is corroborated by the rest of §4 and by the classic sleep-paralysis literature, but before I lean on it in a publication I would open the paper itself.

ClaimEvidence that would change my mind

Turn 9 sharpens what "would change my mind" specifically means for the debris: a measured debris property inconsistent with the Mogul construction — a metal fragment in the Brazel inventory (there was none), an engine, propellers, a recovered mass in the tonnes rather than 2.27 kg, or a field dimension in the kilometres rather than 183 m. Conversely, what would not change my mind is the discovery of more secrecy: the 1994 report states that no air-safety records exist for weather-balloon crashes at all, so "the records are missing" is what a classified-balloon recovery looks like.

Quantified (turn 4, §5.5): one success at $p<10^{-6}$ is worth an LR of $10^6$ and is not sufficient — with the composite evidence LR of $10^{-12}$ and a $10^{-3}$ prior, three independent successes are needed to reach $p\approx1$ (two leave $10^{-3}$; one leaves $10^{-9}$).

9e. Verification log, turn 7 — machine verification of every [CALC]; five of my own defects found and fixed

Method. Turns 1–6 verified numbers by reading sources (open web, Crossref, Wikipedia, NASA PDFs). Turn 7 changed the method: every [CALC] quantity in this document was recomputed numerically in a single node script (116 checks: Simpson quadrature for the complete elliptic integral, IEEE doubles elsewhere, accurate solar-declination model for the polar-day test). The purpose was to test not the literature but my own arithmetic and my own reasoning steps — the two places where a self-verifying loop can silently pass. The MCP search endpoint was re-tested and is still down (Streamable HTTP error); no paywalled source was opened; no new external evidence was gathered.

Result: 111 of 116 checks passed outright. Five turned out to be real defects in my own artefact, and all five are corrected in place above. Four were errors of arithmetic or reasoning; one was a mislabelled magnitude. Two of them made an argument stronger when fixed, which is the useful direction.

Appendix A — Arithmetic behind every [CALC] figure, shown so a reader can re-verify every [CALC] figure by hand.

  1. Equatorial circumference. $2\pi a = 2\pi\times6378.137 = 40{,}075.0$ km.
  2. Meridional circumference. $e^2 = 2f - f^2$, $f = 1/298.257223563$ → $e^2 = 0.00669438$. Quarter meridian $= a\,E(e)$, with $E(e)=\int_0^{\pi/2}\!\sqrt{1-e^2\sin^2\theta}\,d\theta \approx \frac{\pi}{2}\left(1-\frac{e^2}{4}-\frac{3e^4}{64}\right)=\frac{\pi}{2}(1-0.0016736-0.0000021)=1.56816$ → $6{,}378.137\times1.56816=10{,}001.97$ km; meridional circumference $=4\times10.001.97=40{,}007.9$ km. (Cross-check: $2\pi a\times\frac{2}{\pi}E(e)=40{,}075.02\times0.9983243=40{,}007.86$ km.)
  3. Meridional km per degree. Mean over the whole meridian: $40{,}007.9/360 = 111.133$ km/°. The local meridional degree varies from $110.575$ km at the equator ($M(0)=a(1-e^2)=6{,}335.44$ km) to $111.694$ km at the poles ($M(90°)=a/\sqrt{1-e^2}=6{,}399.59$ km) [CALC].
  4. Eratosthenes baseline consistency check (new). At mean latitude ~28° N, $M(28°)=6{,}349.49$ km → 1° = 110.81 km, so the observed $7.2°$ solar-altitude difference implies $7.2\times110.81=798$ km of north–south displacement. The paced baseline of 5,000 stadia corresponds to 787.5 km under the Egyptian stadion (157.5 m) — within 1.3 % — and to 925 km under the Attic stadion (184.98 m), which is +16 %. This localises Eratosthenes' entire known residual error to the stadion convention, not to the geometry.
  5. Horizon distance and dip. $d=\sqrt{2Rh}$; $\delta=\arccos(R/(R+h))\approx\sqrt{2h/R}$.
  6. $h=2$ m: $d=\sqrt{2\times6.371\times10^6\times2}=5048.9$ m; $\delta=\sqrt{4/6.371\times10^6}=7.923\times10^{-4}$ rad $=0.04540°=2.724'$.
  7. $h=11{,}000$ m: $d=374{,}380$ m; $\delta=0.058722$ rad $=3.364°$.
  8. Foucault at Paris. $\sin(48.8566°)=0.75307$; $T=23.9345/0.75307=31.78$ h (sidereal day; 31.87 h if referred to a 24 h solar day).
  9. Lunar horizontal parallax. $\arcsin(R_\oplus/D)=6378.137/384{,}399=0.0165933$ rad $=0.9507°=57.04'$ (3422.6″).

Umbra radius at the Moon. $r_u = R_\oplus - D(R_\odot-R_\oplus)/D_{\odot M}$, $D_{\odot M}=1.496\times10^8+3.844\times10^5=1.49984\times10^8$ km. $(695{,}700-6371)/1.49984\times10^8=0.0045962$. $r_u=6371-384{,}400\times0.0045962=6371-1766.8=4604$ km $=2.650\,R_M$. (The radius spans 4502–4733 km $=2.591$–$2.724\,R_M$ as the Moon runs from apogee to perigee [CALC]; mean 2.650.)

  13. Sunlit regolith vs a mag-6 star — final corrected derivation [CALC]. Solar illuminance at the Moon $E_\odot\approx1.37\times10^5$ lx. Regolith luminance (Lambertian, albedo 0.07–0.16): $L=\rho E_\odot/\pi=3{,}000$–$6{,}900$ cd/m². Film-plane irradiance for the surface at $f/11$: $E_{\rm surf}=\pi L/(4N^2)=19.8$ lx (albedo 0.07) — equivalently $\rho E_\odot/(4N^2)$, because the $\pi$ from the Lambertian law cancels the $\pi$ in the camera equation. A mag-6 star: illuminance at the lens $=1.37\times10^5\times10^{-32.74/2.5}=1.1\times10^{-8}$ lx. Through a 60 mm f/11 Hasselblad (aperture $23.37$ mm²) onto a diffraction-limited Airy core (radius $7.44$ µm, area $174$ µm²), it concentrates to $E_{\star}=E_{\rm star}\,A_{\rm lens}/A_{\rm PSF}=1.5\times10^{-3}$ lx. Ratio $E_{\rm surf}/E_{\star}=1.3\times10^4$ = 13.7 stops. With aberrated spots of $520$–$870$ µm² (realistic hand-held lenses): $4.0\times10^4$–$6.7\times10^4$ = 15.3–16.0 stops. Per-star margins below the surface's mid-density: Sirius (−1.46) 3.8–6.1 stops; mag-0: 5.7–8.1; mag-2: 8.4–10.7; mag-6: 13.7–16.0. Ektachrome SO-368 useful range ≈9–11 stops [LIT], so every star is at or below the grain-noise floor at a surface-exposing exposure. Cross-check via a real exposure law [CALC, corrected turn 7]: the exposure required for correct film density is $H_m = C/\mathrm{ASA}$, with $C=17.6$ lx·s at ISO 100 from the Sunny-16 rule (18 %-grey surface at $10^5$ lx, $f/16$, $1/100$ s) and $C=34.0$ lx·s from the Looney-11 rule (full Moon, ρ=0.12, $f/11$, $1/100$ s). At ASA 160, $f/11$, that puts the proper exposure of the sunlit regolith at 1/93–1/180 s for ρ=0.07 and 1/213–1/412 s for ρ=0.16, i.e. 1/100–1/410 s across the real albedo range — which brackets the flown Hasselblad settings of 1/250–1/500 s within a stop. The same $H_m$ applied to the star gives 75 s (Airy-limited) to ~12 min (870 µm² aberrated) to reach the density the surface reaches in 1/100–1/410 s. Turn-1/turn-3 errors, corrected turn 7: (i) the earlier figure 8.7×10¹¹ (≈40 stops) mixed surface exitance with star illuminance at the lens and ignored diffraction concentration — wrong by ~10⁸ and superseded; (ii) the "independent cross-check" used $t=1/(\mathrm{ASA}\times E)$, which is not a photographic exposure law, produced $3.16\times10^{-4}$ s $=1/3169$ s, and then mislabelled that as "≈1/250–1/500 s" — a 13–32× internal inconsistency; (iii) the "4.2 s" for a mag-6 star to reach mid-density came from the same bad relation and should be 75 s–12 min. The exposure ratio (13.7–16.0 stops) was right throughout, and the corrected cross-check is what validates the 19.8 lx surface figure against the flown shutter settings. The prediction "no stars in the frames" stands and is now derived correctly end-to-end.

Apollo sample mass sum. $21.55+34.35+42.28+76.74+95.71+110.52 = 381.15$ kg under the convention-A masses, and $21.55+33.45+42.80+76.74+95.71+110.52 = 380.77$ kg under convention B. **Turn-7 correction: this is not "consistent with the quoted ≈382 kg total within per-mission rounding" as I wrote in turns 1–6 — per-mission rounding at ±0.005 kg over six missions is worth only ±0.03 kg, whereas the deficits are 0.85 kg (0.22 %) and 1.15 kg (0.30 %)** respectively, always in the same direction (per-mission sum below total). So the residual is a counting convention difference ("collected" vs "weighed/returned"), not measurement error; and since the 382 kg total is primary-confirmed from the NASA-JSC curator's own paper (V-48), the disagreement lives entirely in the per-mission split and cannot touch the total.

  2. Bayes rule. $p(H\mid E)=LR\cdot p/(LR\cdot p + 1 - p)$. Worked examples used in §5.5:
  3. Abduction, composite $LR=10^{-12}$, prior $10^{-3}$: $\frac{10^{-12}\cdot10^{-3}}{10^{-12}\cdot10^{-3}+0.999}=\frac{10^{-15}}{1}\approx10^{-15}$.
  4. Abduction, three blind-signal successes: total $LR=10^{-12}\times10^{18}=10^{6}$; prior $10^{-3}$: $\frac{10^{3}}{10^{3}+1}=0.999$. Two successes: total $LR=10^{0}$: $\frac{10^{-3}}{10^{-3}+0.999}\approx10^{-3}$ — the two successes cancel the $10^{-12}$ composite in odds but the prior still dominates, which is why the honest answer is "three, not one."
  5. Prior required for a 0.5 posterior at $LR=10^{-12}$: solve $LR\cdot p=1-p\Rightarrow p(1+LR)=1$, so $p\approx1$; equivalently the required prior odds $=1/LR=10^{12}\!:\!1$ — unattainable in practice.
  6. Roswell, composite $LR=0.0045$, prior 0.5: $\frac{0.0045\times0.5}{0.0045\times0.5+0.5}=\frac{0.00225}{0.50225}=4.48\times10^{-3}$.
  7. Prior required for a 0.5 posterior at $LR=0.0045$: odds $=1/0.0045=222$, i.e. $p=222/223=99.55\%$.
  8. LR implied by an 85 % posterior from a fair prior: $p=0.15\Rightarrow LR=0.15/0.85=0.176\approx0.18$.

  10. Blind-signal LR. A pre-committed protocol whose false-positive rate is $10^{-6}$ has $P({\rm success}\mid{\rm guessing})=10^{-6}$, so a genuine success carries $LR\approx10^{6}$ against the null. This is the only place in this document where a likelihood ratio is derived from a protocol's own design rather than assigned by judgement.

Excess over the oldest intact terrestrial rock ($\approx4.03$ Ga) $=4.417-4.03=\mathbf{0.387}$ Ga; over the top of the Hadean range ($4.3$ Ga) $=0.117$ Ga; versus the Jack Hills detrital zircons ($\approx4.40$ Ga), the Apollo value is 0.017 Ga younger — but the zircon ages are inherited from recycled crust, whereas 4.417 Ga is a crystallisation age on a specimen nobody possessed before Dec 1972. (Self-audit note, §9f E-6: my first hand-written expectation for this precision was 1369 ppm; the machine computed 1358 ppm and the script's expectation was corrected, exactly as in turn 7's E-1/E-5. Appendix B — Sources and which claims come from where

Ground truth supplied in the brief [GT]: lunar laser retroreflectors on Apollo 11/14/15 still return pulses; Apollo returned ≈382 kg of samples; Area 51 is a real classified USAF facility at Groom Lake, Nevada; Project Mogul was a real classified US balloon programme; the 1997 USAF report "The Roswell Report: Case Closed" attributed the 1947 debris to Project Mogul; Eratosthenes estimated Earth's circumference ~240 BC from shadow angles.

Standard physical/geodetic constants [GT-standard]: speed of light $c = 2.99792458\times10^8$ m/s (exact by SI definition); WGS 84 geodetic parameters; Sun and Moon radii; mean lunar distance.

Appendix C — Reproducibility note

All [CALC] values in Appendix A are hand arithmetic from [GT-standard] constants and can be re-checked without any tooling, and all of them were additionally recomputed numerically in turn 3. Claims that are not [CALC] are attributed above. No measured value in this document was invented, and the items remaining in the Appendix B list are the only places where I knowingly quote a number I could not verify.

Session limits, stated plainly. Turn 1 had no network and no compute kernel; turns 3–4 had node v24.13.0 plus live network to Crossref and Wikipedia but no working MCP search endpoint (and no MCP compute kernel); turns 5, 6, 7 and 8 each confirmed the MCP search and compute endpoints are still down (Streamable HTTP error; the node REPL kernel also failed to start in turn 8) and used the shell's live egress directly — plus pdftotext — against open NASA, Crossref, Wikipedia and NTRS resources. So this run never opened a paywalled full text, and it did not have to: turn 6 closed the last number that turn 5 had reported as paywall-blocked, by finding that the Apollo crew doses are published in the open public record (NASA SP-368 Table 2) rather than only in the paywalled Benton/Science/Health Physics papers. Turn 7 changed the verification method from "read a source" to "recompute": a single node script re-derived all 116 [CALC] quantities, found five defects in my own prior turns' output (§9e), and added one new decisive test to claim (a). Turn 8 used the same egress channel systematically rather than opportunistically, mining a dedicated third-party-evidence source to retire the last flagged item in claim (b) and adding a positive naturalistic result for claim (d). The residual limits of this run are now narrow and stated: the DTIC counterpart of the Benton et al. study (AD-0711316) is publicly catalogued but returned HTTP 403 to my client, so it is located but unread and I quote nothing from it; the two ≤2.6 % Apollo 12/14 sample-mass convention conflicts remain open (their resolution needs the Papike et al. 1998 per-mission table); the 2021 lucid-dream emulation paper is cited at second hand only. No number in this document is fabricated: every [CALC] is re-derivable by hand from Appendix A and has been recomputed numerically by script (§9e, §9f), every [GT] came in the brief, and every [LIT] carries a citation that I have either read in an open source or explicitly flagged as unread. For (c) and (d) the decisive deficit is the absence of a published specimen or a passed identifying test, which no paywall change would alter.

What turn 7 did not do: it did not open any new external source (the MCP search endpoint is still down and no paywall was touched), it did not add a new field observation, and it did not close the two sample-mass convention conflicts. What it did do — and what turns 1–6 could not do — is audit my own reasoning and arithmetic mechanically, which is where the remaining silent-failure risk lived. Five defects were found and fixed; 111 checks passed clean. The audit is repeatable: the scripts verify7.js, verify7b.js and verify7c.js are left in the working directory.

Turn 9's residual limits, stated plainly. The two USAF reports were read as OCR text, not as page images, so I have not verified them against the printed page; an OCR mis-read of a digit is possible, and I checked the figures that matter for internal consistency (the 10-day gap between the 4 June launch and the 14 June find, the 43-flight/67-dummy counts, the 11 crewmen) but not character by character. I did not open the 33 attachments to the 1994 report or the appendices to the 1997 report — I read the main text plus the transcripts and attachment references within it. The two ≤2.6 % Apollo sample-mass convention conflicts remain open (their resolution needs the Papike et al. 1998 per-mission table). The 2021 lucid-dream emulation paper is still second-hand: the Int. J. Dream Research site is behind an Anubis proof-of-work anti-bot challenge and Semantic Scholar rate-limited my requests, and I did not attempt to defeat either, so claim (d)'s one positive experimental item remains flagged as unread in §7 and is load-bearing for nothing. What turn 9 did change is the grade of the Roswell evidence: it is the first claim in this document whose key numbers come from a primary government report read end to end rather than through secondary literature.

What turn 4 did not do: no new experiment, no new field observation, no clinical or radiological data, and — despite turn 9 now having opened the primary Roswell reports — no access at that time to any primary 1947 archive. The Bayesian section (§5.5) is arithmetic over judgement-assigned likelihood ratios and is labelled as such wherever it appears; turn 9 changed the evidence grade of three Roswell inputs without changing §5.5's method.

What turn 9 did not do: it did not touch claims (a), (b) or (d); it did not re-run the 116 turn-7 checks (they passed and are not re-derived here); and it did not resolve the residual that matters, because it cannot — the 1947 debris is gone, and no archive search recovers a specimen that was never preserved.
